fact: The Libyan national standards centre reports that Tunisia's delegation at the 20th Libya-Tunisia working group on mutual recognition of conformity certificates was headed by the Institut national de la normalisation et de la propriete industrielle (INNORPI), which it treats as Tunisia's national standards institute; the document does not mention the law that set it up or any IT standard.

INNORPI, the Institut National de la Normalisation et de la Propriete Industrielle, issued standardization bulletin no. 441 on 25 May 2026 opening a two-month public enquiry on draft Tunisian standards under law 38-2009 and decree 2011-1083; the drafts (measurement, quality management, electrical and fibre-optic cable standards) include no information technology, information security, software or data standard.
